item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
[Image: Triangle with sides 8 cm, 10 cm, and 12 cm]

Which of the following triangles is similar to the triangle shown above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Triangle with sides 10 cm, 12 cm, and 15 cm]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Triangle with sides 10 cm, 12 cm, and 14 cm]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm, and 12 cm]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Triangle with sides 16 cm, 20 cm, and 24 cm]

item.figure_description:
At the top is a triangle with side lengths labeled 8 cm on the left, 10 cm on the right, and 12 cm on the horizontal bottom.
Option A shows a triangle with sides labeled 12 cm on the upper-left, 10 cm on the lower-left, and 15 cm on the right vertical side.
Option B shows a triangle with sides labeled 10 cm on the left, 14 cm along the top, and 12 cm on the bottom-right.
Option C shows an obtuse triangle with sides labeled 6 cm along the horizontal bottom, 8 cm on the right, and 12 cm on the top-left.
Option D shows a triangle with sides labeled 24 cm on the left vertical side, 16 cm on the top-right, and 20 cm on the bottom-right.
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The figure represents two similar triangles. The triangles are not drawn to scale.

[Image: Triangles ABC and DEF]

In the actual triangle ABC, what is the length of side BC?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two right triangles are shown side by side:
- On the left is triangle ABC: vertical leg AB on the left, horizontal base BC on the bottom, with vertex B at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse AC is labeled "6 cm". Inside angle A is labeled "50°" and inside angle C is labeled "40°".
- On the right is a larger triangle DEF: vertical leg DE on the left, horizontal base EF on the bottom labeled "15 cm", with vertex E at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse DF is labeled "20 cm". Inside angle D is labeled "50°" and inside angle F is labeled "40°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Two of the triangles below are similar.

[Image: Four triangles labeled I, II, III, IV]

Which two triangles are similar?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four triangles displayed side by side:
- Triangle I: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal base at the bottom. The top vertex is closer to the left, so the left side is shorter than the right side.
- Triangle II: An acute isosceles triangle with a horizontal top edge. The two longer sides point downward to meet at a sharp vertex at the bottom.
- Triangle III: A tall, thin obtuse triangle with a short horizontal base at the bottom. The left side slants steeply upward to a top vertex, which connects via a long hypotenuse-like side down to the right end of the base.
- Triangle IV: A scalene obtuse triangle with a horizontal top edge, pointing downward to a vertex at the bottom offset to the right. It has the same shape and internal angles as Triangle I, but rotated 180° and reduced in size.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.stem:
This table shows temperatures at various times on four days.

| TEMPERATURE | | | | | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| | 6 a.m. | 9 a.m. | Noon | 3 p.m. | 6 p.m. |
| Monday | 15° | 17° | 24° | 21° | 16° |
| Tuesday | 20° | 16° | 15° | 10° | 9° |
| Wednesday | 8° | 14° | 16° | 19° | 15° |
| Thursday | 8° | 11° | 19° | 26° | 20° |

[Image: Thermometer]

On which day and at what time was the temperature shown in the table the same as that shown on the thermometer?
reference_items.figure_description: A vertical thermometer labeled "Thermometer" at the bottom. The scale on the right has labeled marks at 5°, 10°, 15°, 20°, 25°, 30°, 35°, and 40°, with individual 1-degree tick marks between them. The shaded column of liquid inside the thermometer reaches exactly 24° (one tick mark below 25°).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A shaded rectangle that is 6 cm by 16 cm. Part of the rectangle is unshaded. The unshaded part of the rectangle forms a right triangle on the left that is 6 centimeters by 8 centimeters.]

In the figure above, what is the area of the shaded region in cm^2?
reference_items.figure_description: A rectangle with a height of 6 cm and a total length of 16 cm along the top, both labeled with dimension arrows. An unshaded right triangle occupies the bottom-left portion of the rectangle; its vertical leg is the left side of the rectangle (6 cm) and its horizontal leg along the bottom has a length of 8 cm labeled with a dimension arrow. The remainder of the rectangle is shaded solid black.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Large right triangle divided into smaller triangles]

In the figure above, each of the smaller triangles has the same area. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area?
reference_items.figure_description:
A large right triangle with its vertical leg on the left and horizontal leg at the bottom, divided into smaller congruent right triangles arranged in 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns:
- Row 4 (top): Column 1 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its right angle at the bottom-left and its hypotenuse along the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
- Row 3: Column 1 contains a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 2 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 2: Columns 1 and 2 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 3 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 1 (bottom): Columns 1, 2, and 3 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 4 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Triangular prism]

Which of these could be folded to make a shape like the 3-D figure above?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles connected in a V-shape by two triangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles and two triangles on the right]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Net with three rectangles and three triangles]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Net with three stacked rectangles, one triangle on the top right and one triangle on the bottom left]

reference_items.figure_description:
The stem shows a 3-D triangular prism resting horizontally on one rectangular face, with dashed lines indicating the three hidden edges. The options show four candidate nets:
- Option A: A central horizontal rectangle with an isosceles triangle attached to each vertical side, and another rectangle attached to the outer edge of each triangle angled upward, forming an open V-shape.
- Option B: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with two identical triangles attached to the right edges of the top and middle rectangles, both pointing right.
- Option C: Two congruent rectangles stacked vertically, each having a triangle attached to its left edge pointing left; a third rectangle extends to the right from the top rectangle, ending with a triangle pointing right.
- Option D: Three congruent rectangles stacked vertically in a column, with one triangle attached to the right edge of the top rectangle pointing right, and another triangle attached to the left edge of the bottom rectangle pointing left.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: A ruler with a wavy string above it]

If the string in the diagram is pulled straight, which of these is closest to its length?
reference_items.figure_description: A metric ruler marked from 0 to 11 cm, with ticks at every centimeter and half-centimeter, labeled 'cm' at the left end and with numbers 1 through 11. Above the ruler, a curved line labeled 'string' begins at the 3 cm mark, extends horizontally to approximately 5.5 cm, loops back leftward to about 4.7 cm, and then extends horizontally rightward, ending near the 7 cm mark.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: Which shape has a line of symmetry?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: A trapezoid with two parallel horizontal lines. The right side of the trapezoid is longer than the left hand side.]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: An isosceles triangle with the base forming a vertical line.]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: A parallelogram where top and bottom sides are equal in length and the left and right sides are also equal in length.]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: A right triangle with the 90 degree angle in the bottom left.]

reference_items.figure_description:
Four geometric shapes labeled A through D:
A: A trapezoid with horizontal top and bottom parallel sides; the bottom is longer than the top, and the right slanted side is longer and less steep than the left side.
B: An isosceles triangle with a vertical base on the left and a vertex pointing to the right; the top and bottom sides are marked with equal tick marks.
C: A parallelogram with horizontal top and bottom sides each marked with a single tick mark, and slanted left and right sides each marked with a double tick mark.
D: A scalene right-angled triangle with a vertical left side and a horizontal bottom side, with a right-angle square symbol marked at the lower-left corner.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
